websiteDepartments.name: ICT & Computer Science
websiteDepartments.shortDescription: TVET CDACC & KNEC-accredited software engineering, networking, cybersecurity, and database administration programmes.
websiteDepartments.overview: The Department of ICT & Computer Science prepares industry-ready software engineers, network architects, cloud administrators, and cybersecurity practitioners through hands-on project laboratories and structured industrial attachments across Kenya’s technology sector.

websiteDepartments.campusName: Nairobi Main Campus & Westlands Technology Park

programmes.title: Diploma in Information Communication Technology (DICT Level 6)
programmes.entryRequirements: KCSE Mean Grade C- (Minus) or Certificate in ICT Level 5

programmes.title: Certificate in Information Communication Technology (CICT Level 5)
Diploma in Cyber Security & Digital Forensics
programmes.entryRequirements: KCSE Mean Grade C- (Minus) with C- in English and Mathematics

facilities: Cisco & MikroTik Enterprise Networking Rack Laboratory
High-speed redundant fiber campus intranet and digital resource repository
learningOutcomes: Architect and deploy secure full-stack web, mobile, and enterprise applications.
Administer Linux/Windows server infrastructure and relational PostgreSQL databases.
Configure switched/routed enterprise networks and perform security vulnerability audits.

announcements.title: May & September 2026 DICT Level 6 Applications Open
announcements.summary: Practical lab induction and coding bootcamp included for all new Level 5 & Level 6 entrants.

faqs.question: Do trainees need their own laptops from day one?
faqs.answer: Every ICT student receives scheduled workstation access in our Nairobi and Westlands laboratories. Personal laptops are helpful for home practice but are not mandatory for practical assessments.

faqs.question: Is industrial attachment included in the Diploma programme?
faqs.answer: Yes. All Level 6 Diploma trainees complete a supervised 12-week industrial attachment prior to graduation.
